Definition: from G1223 and a derivative of G4192; to toil through, i.e. (passively) be worried:--be grieved.
BiblicalUsage: This word means to be grieved or worn out by trouble, and the form in the text is the middle voice of the same verb. The apostles are grieved because Peter and John teach the resurrection, and Paul is grieved by the spirit that follows the slave girl, until he turns and commands it out.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe grief at the truth being opposed is a holy thing; the apostles were grieved because men could not bear to hear of the resurrection, and Paul's grief ended in deliverance, which is where all holy grief should lead.
